calendar.impact: First EIA weekly print with the Isaias shut-in week in it (Gulf shut-ins peaked at 71.5% Friday, down to 29.63% Monday); the PADD 2 detail arbitrates the remaining Whiting Pipestill 11C/FCCU 500 question. IEA monthly report lands the same day, one day after OPEC cut 2026 demand growth to 400 kb/d.

calendar.impact: Bids went in Oct 6 (11:00 a.m. CT); a clean award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery. No award announced yet. Separately, DOE authorized a 4 Mbbl emergency SPR exchange Oct 10 (2 Mbbl each to ExxonMobil, BP America) for Isaias disruptions.
calendar.title: SPR 40-million-barrel exchange award (pending)

changes.balance: The war premium has two-way risk with the balance tipping physical. Monday faded the ceasefire entirely and paid for escalation (Brent settle the highest since Sep 15), while the overnight softness is the diesel leg trading Russian supply talk, still with no loadings. Bulls hold a constricting Strait, a closed Riyadh airport with a promised Saudi response, a seven-day $100-plus crack, and light WTI length. Bears hold Novak's volume comments, OPEC's demand downgrade at the back of the curve, a fast Isaias restart, and heavy Brent length into any genuine de-escalation.
changes.body: Russia hit at least six Ukrainian energy targets on Monday, and Zelenskiy said Moscow is unwilling to accept the energy ceasefire announced Sunday and intends to continue its attacks. Trump insisted Monday the agreement stands and said Putin wants a deal more than Zelenskiy. The market faded the announcement on Monday: Brent Dec26 settled at $106.65, its highest settle since September 15, and WTI Nov26 settled at $93.74, both up roughly $2. Overnight Tuesday the tape gave back $1.69 on WTI and $1.58 on Brent (WTI Nov26 $92.05, Brent Dec26 $105.07 as of about 02:06 MDT), with Asia desks naming the prospect of additional Russian diesel supply. In the Gulf, the IRGC says a third supertanker was struck Monday morning in the Strait (claim not independently confirmed); UKMTO counted 11 attacks in the week ending Oct 9, with Hormuz traffic about 75% below pre-conflict levels. Riyadh airport stayed closed all Monday with no reopening date, and the Saudi energy minister said the response must be equally serious.
changes.conditional: A Russian diesel cargo loads -> the diesel leg breaks and the pullback extends; a Saudi response or a strike on Saudi oil facilities -> the premium rebuilds fast
changes.delta: Ceasefire rejected in fact Monday (six Ukrainian energy targets hit; Kyiv says Moscow will not accept it); Monday settles WTI $93.74 / Brent $106.65 (highest Brent settle since Sep 15); overnight tape -$1.69 WTI / -$1.58 Brent on Russian diesel prospects; IRGC claims a third tanker struck Monday in Hormuz; Riyadh airport closed all Monday, Saudi response promised
changes.source: Reuters via yalibnan.com, Oct 13, 2026; Reuters via angelone.in, Oct 13, 2026; in-house quotes pull, Oct 13, 2026, 02:06 MDT; PressTV, Oct 12, 2026; WPC Energy Congress reporting, Oct 12, 2026
changes.title: Ceasefire rejected in fact; Monday rallied on the war, Tuesday fades on diesel talk

changes.balance: The diesel paper now has a Russian supply advocate (Novak) but still no cargoes, and it is selling into physical diesel stocks at a 44-year seasonal low with the crack seven days above $100. OPEC's demand cut is a deferred-curve weight, not a prompt one: the front is priced on physical tightness and war risk. The first loading and Wednesday's EIA print are the next facts.
changes.body: The diesel crack reads $104.46 on the latest validated bar (history refreshed Oct 13): the seventh consecutive day above $100 (35 total days; all-time max $117.92, Sep 16). The 3-2-1 reads $61.03 (max $75.31, Aug 28). Deputy PM Novak said Monday Russia could return diesel exports to levels above those Trump outlined. No loading has been reported; the license names no volumes or buyers, the 2022 statutory import ban objection stands, and Moscow's own export ban runs through October. OPEC's monthly report cut 2026 global demand growth to 400 kb/d from 1.4 Mb/d (FXEmpire summary, Oct 13); the IEA monthly follows Wednesday.
changes.conditional: First Russian diesel loading -> crack leg breaks; no loadings plus Hormuz escalation -> $100+ regime extends
changes.delta: Diesel crack $104.46 (seventh straight day above $100, not a record); Novak says Russian diesel exports could exceed the outlined levels; still no loadings; OPEC cuts 2026 demand growth to 400 kb/d from 1.4 Mb/d
changes.source: Validated crack history, refreshed Oct 13, 2026; Reuters via yalibnan.com, Oct 13, 2026; OPEC monthly report via FXEmpire summary, Oct 13, 2026
changes.title: Diesel crack holds $100+ for a seventh day; OPEC cuts demand growth

changes.balance: Canada gets no new price signal until today's session trades: Monday's settles carried Friday's strip tick for tick. The freight regime is unmoved (TD3C WS 1058, TD9 WS 681, age-labeled), so global sour tightness still cannot transmit to the diff, and the November apportionment notice (about Oct 19) remains the next real observation. Operationally the basin is healing on schedule, which softens SYN against WCS into late October even while freight holds heavy wide.
changes.body: Canadian diffs (ICE, Oct 12, holiday-thin): TMW Nov26 -$24.78 and Dec26 -$25.60, both unchanged on zero volume; ARV Nov26 -$15.84 (+$0.20); ARV-TMW November +$8.94, the implied export arb. SYN Nov26 +$6.46, C5 Dec26 +$6.00, both unchanged. Isaias restart: MMA Monday put Gulf oil shut-ins at 29.63% (604,503 b/d), down from 71.5% Friday, with 5 platforms still evacuated. August ST53 (pulled Oct 12): thermal about 2.10 MMb/d, Firebag a record 252.3 kb/d, Foster Creek a record 248.5 kb/d, no turnaround signatures. Suncor Edmonton and Base Plant fall work ends Oct 13 on the union schedule; Horizon implies completion about Oct 12 to 13; Syncrude wraps Oct 16.
changes.conditional: Today's ICE session trades -> first real Canadian price discovery since Friday; November apportionment notice (about Oct 19) binds -> December wide extends
changes.delta: TMW Nov26 -$24.78 / Dec26 -$25.60 (ICE, Oct 12; unchanged, zero volume, holiday carry); ARV-TMW Nov +$8.94; Gulf shut-ins down to 29.63% Monday (MMA); August ST53 records at Firebag and Foster Creek
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 12, 2026; MMA (BSEE), Oct 12, 2026; AER ST53 August 2026, pulled Oct 12, 2026
changes.title: No Canadian price discovery Monday; Isaias restart halves shut-ins again

flags.body: Russia hit at least six Ukrainian energy targets on Monday and Kyiv says Moscow will not accept the announced ceasefire; Trump insists it stands. Novak says Russian diesel exports could exceed the outlined levels, but no cargo has loaded under the arrangement. The crack is seven days above $100 against US diesel stocks at a record seasonal low.
flags.title: Ceasefire rejected in fact; diesel loadings still the break point
flags.trigger: A Russian diesel cargo loads, or Moscow confirms a halt to energy strikes in behavior (not statements)

flags.body: The Oct 12 ICE Canadian settles are a holiday carry (TMW unchanged on zero volume), so the strip carries no new information until today's session. Riyadh airport remained closed through Monday with no reopening date, and the Saudi energy minister promised a serious response that had not been announced as of this run.
flags.title: Holiday-thin ICE settles; Saudi response unannounced
flags.trigger: Today's ICE settles print with volume, or Saudi Arabia announces its response

flags.body: No DOE award announcement as of early Tuesday, a week after the Oct 6 bid deadline. The award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery when it lands.
